name: Jennu Kurumba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Upadhyaya, U. P. (1971). Coorg Kannada (Jenu Kuruba Dialect). Linguistic Survey of India Series 9. Poona: Deccan College Postgraduate and Research Institute. 8+88 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID Old Widener 3254.1.7 vol.9 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Nothing. Section 1 Phonology (pp. 1-8: 1.1 inventory, 1.2 selected contrasts, 1.3 allophonic description, 1.4 clusters) never mentions stress, accent, prominence or intonation (grep of the full scanned text: only 'mistress' in the vocabulary). Only prosodic remark: 'A short vowel occurring in the final position is half-long phonetically' (p. 2). Data from Jenu Kurubas of Nanjarajapatna, Coorg, recorded 1967.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 langdoc list for jenn1240 (35 entries, fetched sources as CSV) and Glottolog reference 557733 = Varghese, Bijumon (2015) The Tribes of Palakkad, Kerala: A Sociolinguistic Profile, SIL ESR 2015-028 (cited only for subclassification; covers Irula/Muduga/Attapady Kurumba etc., not Jenu Kurumba proper).
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic listing only. Remaining Glottolog entries are ethnographic (Bird-David, Demmer, Misra, Fürer-Haimendorf, Menon, Fuchs, Luiz, Shashi, Bhanu, Naveh) and were not pursued.

sources.citation: Zvelebil, Kamil V. (1980). Jēnu Kurumba: First Report on a Tribal Language of the Nilgiri Area. Proceedings of the Sixth Annual Meeting of the Berkeley Linguistics Society, 111-119. DOI 10.3765/bls.v6i0.2114
sources.note: Nothing. §2.1 'phonological features' (pp. 112-114) covers contrastive vowel centralization, nasalized vowels, v->b, *p->h->0, retained k- before front vowels, a nasalized bilabial fricative semivowel, *-d->-r-, palatalization of -d-/-dd-/-nn-; no mention of stress or accent. Data from Kadu Nayika (Kattu Nayaka) elephant mahouts at Teppakadu, Mudumalai, Nilgiris.
